question: Which of the following best defines an antiseptic?

options.A: A chemical agent applied to non-living surfaces to destroy spores
options.B: An antimicrobial substance applied to living tissue to reduce infection
options.C: A systemic antibiotic used to treat bacterial pneumonia
options.D: A physical method of sterilization using pressurized steam

explanation: Antiseptics are specifically formulated for application to living tissues, like skin, to prevent infection, unlike disinfectants which are used on inanimate objects. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h1)

question: Why should disinfectants never be applied directly to a patient's open wound?

options.A: They are completely ineffective against bacteria on skin
options.B: They are too dilute to have any antimicrobial effect
options.C: They are too toxic and caustic, leading to tissue damage and burns
options.D: They neutralize the effects of subsequent antibiotic therapy

explanation: Disinfectants are harsh chemical agents meant only for non-living surfaces; applying them to living tissue causes severe chemical burns and toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h1)

question: What is a primary mechanism of action of alcohols on microorganisms?

options.B: Dissolution of lipid membranes and protein denaturation

explanation: Alcohols function by dissolving the lipid-rich components of microbial cell membranes and denaturing vital proteins, causing cell lysis. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h2)

question: How do halogens such as iodine and chlorine typically destroy microorganisms?

options.A: By oxidizing cellular components and inhibiting enzymatic systems
options.B: By acting as a physical barrier against nutrient absorption
options.C: By increasing the structural rigidity of the peptidoglycan wall
options.D: By promoting rapid sporulation in vegetative bacteria

explanation: Halogens exert their antimicrobial effects primarily through oxidation of essential cellular components and the inhibition of critical enzymatic systems. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h2)

question: Which chemical class is known for providing persistent residual antimicrobial action on the skin and is commonly used for surgical hand scrubs?
explanation: Biguanides, such as chlorhexidine, bind strongly to the stratum corneum, providing sustained residual antimicrobial activity on the skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h3)

question: What is a major limitation of using alcohols as antiseptics?

options.A: They act too slowly to be clinically useful
options.B: They stain the skin permanently yellow
options.C: They lack activity against bacterial spores
options.D: They are corrosive to human tissue

explanation: While alcohols are fast-acting against vegetative bacteria and many viruses, they are not sporocidal and cannot destroy bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h3)

question: Why is pre-cleaning to remove organic matter essential before applying a disinfectant?

options.A: Organic matter enhances the penetration of the chemical agent
options.B: Blood and pus can bind or neutralize the active chemical ingredients
options.C: Organic matter accelerates the sporocidal activity of all disinfectants
options.D: It prevents the disinfectant from evaporating too quickly

explanation: Organic material like blood and pus can bind to or neutralize chemical disinfectants, significantly reducing their ability to kill microorganisms. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following groups of microorganisms is the most resistant to chemical disinfection and antisepsis?
explanation: Bacterial spores possess thick, impermeable coats that make them exceptionally resistant to standard chemical disinfectants and antiseptics. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h4)

question: What is a crucial nursing action when applying an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Wiping the hands with a sterile towel immediately after application
options.B: Rubbing the hands together until the solution is completely dry
options.C: Rinsing the hands under cold running water to remove chemical residue
options.D: Diluting the rub with sterile water if the skin feels dry

explanation: Alcohol-based hand rubs must be allowed to evaporate fully through continuous friction until dry to achieve their maximum antimicrobial efficacy. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h5)

question: Before applying an iodine-based antiseptic for a surgical prep, what vital assessment must the nurse perform?

options.A: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate
options.B: Assess the patient for a history of seafood or iodine allergies
options.C: Determine the patient's last meal intake
options.D: Verify the patient's tetanus immunization status

explanation: Nurses must assess for iodine or shellfish allergies prior to using iodine-based antiseptics to prevent severe hypersensitivity and anaphylactoid reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h5)

question: What personal protective equipment is essential when handling strong disinfectants like glutaraldehyde to protect respiratory health?

options.B: Proper room ventilation and appropriate respiratory protection
options.C: An open-face plastic shield without eye protection

explanation: Strong aldehyde vapors can irritate the respiratory tract, making proper ventilation and appropriate respiratory protection mandatory safety requirements. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h6)

question: Why are neonates and infants at a higher risk of systemic toxicity from topical antiseptics?

options.A: Their skin has a higher surface-area-to-mass ratio and increased permeability
options.B: They produce excessive skin oils that bind toxic chemicals
options.C: Infants lack normal flora, making chemicals absorb faster
options.D: Their immature kidneys cannot excrete water

explanation: Neonates possess a high surface-area-to-mass ratio and more permeable skin, increasing systemic absorption and the risk of toxicity from topical agents. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h6)

question: What practice contributes to the development of microbial resistance against antiseptics and disinfectants?

options.A: Adhering strictly to manufacturer dilution guidelines
options.B: Using sub-lethal concentrations and inadequate contact times
options.C: Ensuring organic matter is removed before disinfection
options.D: Rotating cleaning agents according to policy

explanation: Using sub-lethal concentrations or failing to meet required contact times exposes microorganisms to stress without killing them, fostering resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h7)

question: Which measure is a key component of infection control protocols to prevent the spread of resistant organisms?

options.A: Relying solely on chemical wipes without physical cleaning
options.B: Strict compliance with standard precautions and institutional cleaning policies
options.C: Using high-level disinfectants on intact human skin
options.D: Eliminating hand hygiene protocols to save time

explanation: Strict compliance with standard precautions and evidence-based institutional cleaning policies is essential to prevent healthcare-associated infections and resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h7)
